whatItIs.text: A fermented liquid of soybeans, roasted grain, brine, and kōji mould — saltiness and umami in one pour, from China some 2,200 years ago.

historyNote.text: Salty condiments began as a way to stretch expensive salt: Zhou-dynasty cooks fermented fish with it, and by the Han dynasty soybeans led the recipe; the name jiangyou was standard by the Song dynasty (960-1279), and it is listed in bamboo slips from Mawangdui.

howToChoose.text: Naturally brewed (shoyu) beats chemically hydrolysed versions; light for seasoning, dark for colour, tamari if gluten matters — check labels, since wheat is usual.

storage.text: It keeps essentially indefinitely, but flavour fades — refrigerate after opening.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Soy sauce seasons everything from fried rice to caramel-braised chicken; reduce it with sugar and star anise into a glaze, or mix with mayo for a quick dip.
